findings.claim: Duty 5 tells the agent the invoking wrapper has already appended the registry paths to permissions.additionalDirectories and forbids the agent to write them itself. Bootstrap mode says duties 3-7 are identical, but the bootstrap wrapper cmd/bootstrap/run.sh never appends anything. It only reads additionalDirectories to build --repos (L79-84); only routines/smine-nightly/run.sh L298-305 reconciles. So `/smine-orchestrate bootstrap` never reconciles. A repo registered without the additionalDirectories opt-in (a developer-audience add with the checkbox off) stays missing after bootstrap, and the run only reports it. Spec item correctness-60 requires bootstrap mode to run the same reconcile duty.
findings.fix: Append the missing registry paths to additionalDirectories in cmd/bootstrap/run.sh before the orchestrate stage, using the same append-only jq as smine-nightly run.sh L298-305. Alternatively, have L61 name only the nightly wrapper and make bootstrap mode perform the append itself.
findings.evidence: Re-read smine-orchestrate SKILL.md L24 ('duties 3-7 below are identical') and L59-61. Grepped additionalDirectories across routines/, cmd/bootstrap and cmd/sync: the only writer is routines/smine-nightly/run.sh:298-305, and cmd/bootstrap/run.sh:79-84 only reads it. Cross-chunk: the fix may land in cmd/bootstrap/run.sh, which another chunk reviews.

findings.claim: Duty 4 re-syncs a context pack only for repos.json entries 'whose target carries docs/context.json'. sync_context.sh writes the pack's context.json to <target>/<context-dir>/context.json (L211, L325), and context-dir is a supported deploy option (--context-dir, stored as deploy.contextDir). A repo whose pack was deployed with --context-dir context (the layout this repo uses itself) has no docs/context.json. Its pack is therefore never re-synced after a merge, although spec item correctness-59 requires a re-run 'per registry entry with a deployed pack using its recorded options'.
findings.fix: Detect a deployed pack by looking for any <target>/<dir>/context.json that carries a deploy section (deploy.contextDir), not only docs/context.json. Then re-run sync_context.sh with --context-dir <recorded dir> plus the other recorded flags.
findings.evidence: Re-read smine-orchestrate SKILL.md L55-57. In cmd/sync/sync_context.sh: L74-77 auto-discover only docs/context.json unless --context-dir is passed, L109 defaults CONTEXT_DIR to docs, and L211/L325 write the file under $TARGET/$CONTEXT_DIR. A non-docs pack therefore lives where the skill's selector never looks.

findings.claim: The default-deny self-mining exclusion drops sessions whose cwd resolves inside 'the run's repo root (including .claude/worktrees/)'. Nightly mining runs with cwd set to the routine worktree under ~/.cache/claude-routine/worktrees/<group> (smine-nightly run.sh L128-137 cd "$wt"). Read literally, the run's repo root is that worktree, and the operator's interactive sessions in the smine main checkout and its .claude/worktrees/ pool resolve outside it. Those sessions are mined with dev mode off, which is the default on a developer install: run.sh L40-42 turns dev mode on only via SMINE_DEV_MODE or dev-mode: true. Routine sessions are still caught by the claude-routines/ branch test. The interactive smine-repo sessions that correctness-116 and --dev exist to exclude are not.
findings.fix: Define the exclusion root deterministically as the main checkout (`git worktree list --porcelain` first entry, or `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`'s parent), not the cwd's toplevel. State that this holds when the run itself executes in a routine worktree.
findings.evidence: Re-read smine-batch SKILL.md L28 and L42. In routines/smine-nightly/run.sh: L128 creates the worktree, L137 does `cd "$wt"` before stage 1, and L40-42 derive dev mode, off by default. routines/_lib/worktree.sh:20 puts ROUTINE_WT_ROOT outside the main checkout. The bootstrap wrapper runs from repo_root and is unaffected. The exposure cell is 'rare' because how an agent resolves 'the run's repo root' cannot be proven.

findings.claim: The casual-lockout gate in step 4 checks only 'a skills-kind proposal targeting an existing skill'. Two context-kind routes in the same step also edit shipped skill files: (c) an acdsl-context declaration amendment ('declare <entry-ID> in skills/<path>/SKILL.md acdsl-context:', which smine-context and smine-memory both propose), and (d) the eviction 'remove <ID> from <skill> context:', which edits that skill's frontmatter and both version surfaces. smine-orchestrate L41 treats any delta modifying a non-origin: user SKILL.md on a casual install as a hard-invariant breach. Sequence on a casual install: a voted or decide-auto-applied context declaration proposal for a shipped skill → apply edits the skill, archives the proposal to done.md, and the vote is drained (run.sh L284-286) → orchestrate must revert that change or reject the whole run. The user ends up with an 'implemented' proposal whose change was undone, or with a rejected night.
findings.fix: Widen the step-4 lockout to any proposal of any kind whose implementation edits files of a skill lacking origin: user (disposition casual-locked). Have smine-context and smine-memory drop declaration and eviction candidates against non-origin: user skills on casual installs.
findings.evidence: Re-read smine-apply SKILL.md L31: the lockout sentence names skills-kind only, and routes (c)/(d) edit SKILL.md. smine-context SKILL.md L48 and smine-memory SKILL.md L58 propose declaration edits with no casual guard. smine-orchestrate SKILL.md L41 makes the breach a hard invariant. routines/smine-nightly/run.sh L274-291 publishes and drains votes before stage 3.

findings.claim: The Drift stage treats every sessions/<scope>/analyzed-*.txt as a per-dimension ledger and reports ids that are in some but not all of them. This change moved the smine-batch ledger from sessions/analyzed-sessions.txt into each folder as sessions/<name>/analyzed-sessions.txt (smine-batch L36), so the glob now picks it up. That ledger holds every mined id, skipped ghosts included, which must stay in it to prevent re-mining. The dimension ledgers deliberately leave skipped sessions out (smine SKILL.md L44). As a result, every skipped session in every batch, plus every session of a mined-but-unrouted batch, is reported as diverging drift on every run, which buries the partial-failure drift the stage exists to surface.
findings.fix: Restrict the Drift prompt to the five dimension ledgers by name (analyzed-{memory,skill,routines,rules,permissions}.txt) and say explicitly that analyzed-sessions.txt is excluded.
findings.evidence: Re-read session-mine.js L97-107 (the 'sessions/<scope>/analyzed-*.txt files' glob, symmetric difference across them) and smine-batch SKILL.md L36, now sessions/<name>/analyzed-sessions.txt. The base version at b4981b8 has smine-batch L32 'sessions/analyzed-sessions.txt' at the sessions root, outside the per-scope glob. smine SKILL.md L44 says skipped sessions stay out of the dimension ledgers deliberately.
